questions.question: In the HGAB 3rd-reading bridge table, which project has the highest allocation per stated meter?

The chainage may include approaches, and allocation per meter is a screening ratio, not construction unit cost.

questions.question: Burol’s bridge-rate card shows ₱150 million across 25 stated meters. What allocation per stated meter does that work out to?

questions.hint: Divide the allocation by 25.

questions.question: A project beats its peer median by 2×, but stays below Q3 + 1.5× IQR. Does it trigger the high-rate flag?

questions.hint: The rule uses two checks together.

questions.question: A road title gives an 8-meter segment. Which review signal should light up?
questions.explanation: The separate short-range screen flags stated lengths under 10 meters for source review. It asks a human to check the notation and scope.
questions.hint: Eight is below the disclosed 10-meter review threshold.

questions.question: The same positive amount appears 10 times under one PAP across three offices. Which review flag catches this pattern?
questions.explanation: The repeated-amount screen looks for the same positive amount under one PAP across at least three named offices. It highlights a pattern for review; it does not explain why the amounts match.
questions.hint: Look for the flag about an amount appearing again and again.

questions.question: A project has a POW and geotagged photos, but no RDC endorsement. What does the documentation screen call this?

questions.question: A 3rd-reading project has no selected NEP match and no listed documents. Which two review leads apply?

questions.question: Two Rainwater Collector proposals list different locations and materials but the same package allocation. What pattern should catch your eye?

questions.question: Two NEP matching screens return different counts of possible HGAB insertions. What is the best next move?

Choose the larger count as confirmed
Treat every unmatched row as a new project

questions.hint: The disagreement is between the screens, so inspect the rows they treat differently.

questions.question: A multi-purpose building row has no selected NEP counterpart. What should the reviewer compare before calling it new?

questions.explanation: Building titles can vary, so a possible insertion needs a careful counterpart check using location and scope as well as the title.
questions.hint: A reliable match needs more than one text string.

questions.question: A project title recurs in an older GAA. What should be compared before calling the work a duplicate?
questions.explanation: Similar or recurring titles can describe different components or locations. The summary treats recurrence as a lead to check against funded scope and station ranges.
questions.hint: Check whether it is the same place and the same funded segment.

questions.question: Road and flood allocations of exactly ₱5 million cluster in some of the same offices. What does that finding describe?
choices: An added flag on every project
questions.explanation: The observed association is at office level. It is not an extra individual-project flag and does not establish why the allocation pattern occurs.
questions.hint: Keep the conclusion at the same level as the data pattern.

questions.question: A large named appropriation returns in the budget. Which record would best explain its full history?

questions.answer: A whole-project cost and completion ledger
questions.explanation: A whole-project ledger can show prior appropriations, cumulative costs, completed components, and what remains to be funded.
questions.hint: Follow the project from its first appropriation through completion.

questions.question: A project has no supported segment length. What should the cost-per-meter screen do?
questions.explanation: Without a supported length, an allocation-per-meter rate cannot be calculated. The missing denominator is an evidence gap, not a zero-length project.
questions.hint: A rate needs a defensible denominator.

questions.question: A bridge ranks high per stated meter. What should a reviewer check before interpreting that ratio?

questions.answer: Funded span, approaches, and project quantities
